positions.reasoning: Official count has Flavio leading Lula by only about 3 points (47 to 44 with 98 percent counted), a much narrower gap than the first partial counts suggested, and multiple post-first-round sources (CNBC, NPR) call the October 25 runoff roughly even while Kalshi prices Lula at 41 to 42 cents. Polymarket's own 16 cent ask looks like an overreaction to the first-round shock headlines rather than a reasoned runoff forecast.

closed.question: Will Lula win the most votes in the first round of the 2026 Brazil presidential election?
closed.reasoning: AtlasIntel (Sept 29, n=5005, MoE 1pt) has Lula at 45.3-46.2% vs Flavio 42.2-43.1%; Datafolha (Oct 1) has Lula 45% vs Flavio 40%; Quaest (Sept 28) has Lula 39% vs Flavio 34%. All three major pollsters agree Lula leads the first-round vote count by 3 to 6 points, but the market prices Lula to win the first round at only 62 cents, which undervalues that consistent lead even after discounting for Brazil's history of underestimating right-wing turnout.
